liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Fire On The Mountain** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls this Fire On The Mountain extremely powerful and asks whether any version beats it; Reviewer considers this Fire On The Mountain close to the best in quite some time [19][20]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Reviewer calls the Scarlet Begonias into Fire On The Mountain excellent, with Brent playing standout keyboards [15]
- **Lost Sailor** (1 review): Reviewer loves that the second set opens with Lost Sailor into Saint Of Circumstance [17]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd81-08-31 s1t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd81-08-31 s1t02 Feel Like A Stranger**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd81-08-31 s1t03 Jack-A-Roe**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd81-08-31 s1t04 El Paso**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd81-08-31 s1t05 Candyman**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd81-08-31 s1t06 Little Red Rooster**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd81-08-31 s1t07 Loser**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd81-08-31 s1t08 Cassidy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-08-31.144666.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 26 songs; 182 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd81-08-31.sbd.miller.30070.sbeok.flacf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 185 min; rated 4.33/5 by 6 [3]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sounds good, similar to an older tape the reviewer owned but cleaner; Soundboard is incomplete; the first two minutes of Stranger come from a rough audience recording [15][16]
- **gd81-08-31.aud.munder.9619.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 185 min; rated 4.14/5 by 7 [7]. Said about its sound: Reviewer found this audience recording badly sounding and recommends it only to completists; Reviewer describes the audience recording as warm and clear, with a pleasant room atmosphere [12][14]
- **gd1981-08-31.153344.nak304.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 177 min [9]

## Around the show

- Attendee says the Aladdin had good acoustics but was later demolished [13]
- Attendee says the hotel shared the building, and the band briefly mingled with the audience there [13]
- Attendee describes a small venue, sitting in the first row at the back [18]
- Attendee recalls two Las Vegas shows before the band moved on to the Silver Bowl [18]
- Attendee ranks it among the best early Las Vegas shows by the band [13]
- Better than the previous night, with tighter playing and stronger vocals; Bob seems recovered from the 30th [16]
- Second-set song selection differs from what the band typically played on most nights of this period [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-08-31.144666.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mark Severson's Master Audience Cassettes; (3) x Nakamichi 700 mics (left/right cardioids, omni center)> Custom mixer by Jamie Poris > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell MX90) [1]. Also: Master cassettes came from Mark Severson; Charlie Miller made the transfer, with pitch correction help from Joe B. Jones; An 11-second patch in Drums comes from a Sennheiser 421 source supplied by Frank Streeter and Miller [1]
- **gd81-08-31.sbd.miller.30070.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard [3]. Also: Soundboard is patched with audience source at the start of Stranger and from mid-Morning Dew to the end; Source discs came from Joe Browning; disc changes are seamless [3]
- **gd81-08-31.aud.munder.9619.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [7]
- **gd1981-08-31.153344.nak304.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassette; Nakamichi 300 mics + CP4 capsules > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell UDXLIIS) [9]. Also: Nakamichi 700 source supplies a 6:40 patch in Drums and a short patch in the Morning Dew to Playin' transition [9]

## Art and photos

- Poster by John Rottet Grateful Dead: [1981-08-31 Aladdin Theater, Las Vegas, NV, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1981-08-31-aladdin-theater-las-vegas-nv-usa/) [25]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Aladdin Theatre - August 31, 1981](https://www.dead.net/show/august-31-1981) [26]
